one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window (Q2 FY27 reports ~mid-December 2026). Scheduled events inside 2026-10-05..11-04: hyperscaler Q3 prints and 2027 capex commentary (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN, ~Oct 28-30), which feed the AI-demand narrative; possible further ATM/debt issuance (Oracle sold $20B of equity via ATM in Q1 and filings point to ~$40B more financing in FY27); rating-agency commentary (Moody's Baa2 negative outlook) at any time. The Project Jupiter air-permit decision (Nov 23) and the class-action briefing deadline (Dec 18) fall just outside. The stock is already down ~56% from its high and sits near technical support (~$136-143); a downgrade to junk or a large new equity raise is the main left-tail risk, while strong hyperscaler capex guides are the upside. With no company-specific scheduled catalyst I keep a near-symmetric lognormal around ~$142 (tiny negative tilt for continued supply of stock from ATM issuance) with monthly sigma ~15.5% (56%/3.5 = 16%).

fair_value.method: Blend of 0.6 x forward P/E (skeptic-haircut CY2028 EPS ~$10.6 x 14x = ~$148) and 0.4 x skeptic DCF (~$101 one year out, after dilution and ~$89B net debt) = ~$129.

bear.story: OpenAI cannot fund its ~$60B/yr compute bill and stretches or restructures the Oracle contract; RPO conversion slips, Project Jupiter and other sites delayed; Moody's/S&P cut to junk, financing costs jump and Oracle issues more equity. CY2027 EPS ~$8 on more shares, market pays ~10x.

base.story: OCI grows strongly (RPO converts roughly on schedule) but FCF stays negative through FY28, dilution continues, credit stays BBB- with negative outlooks; the stock trades ~13-14x forward EPS, below software and hyperscaler peers.

bull.story: AI demand holds through 2027 (hyperscaler capex guides up again), OCI margins hit the 35-40% target, prepayments and 'bring your own hardware' deals cut net capex, leverage peaks and spreads tighten; rerates toward ~19-20x on ~$11.5 CY2028 EPS.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: ORCL trades at 14.6x CY2027 EPS vs peer median 21.0x; we apply 14x to Oct-2027 forward EPS after a 16% haircut, i.e. a ~33% discount to the median but inside the range (near CRM 14.3x, WDAY 14.2x).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount, argued to persist through the horizon: (1) free cash flow negative through at least FY28 by company capex guide ($90-95B gross FY27) vs peers that self-fund; (2) balance sheet: ~$125B debt, BBB- (S&P) / Baa2 negative (Moody's), CDS ~200bp vs ~80bp for peers, 2055 bonds near 77c; (3) customer concentration: ~half of $664B RPO from OpenAI, which itself needs ~$200B of outside capital; (4) mix shift to 30-40% gross-margin AI infrastructure. These are structural for 12 months, not sentiment.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$95 (about 9.6x CY2027 consensus EPS) the market would be pricing a fundamental break rather than volatility: a cut to high-yield, an OpenAI contract restructuring/cancellation, or an equity raise large enough to impair per-share earnings. My base case assumes credit stays investment grade and RPO converts; a sustained move there means one of those has failed.

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Q1 FY27 (primary filing) was strong on growth (rev +30%, OCI +121%, RPO $664B) but cash flow is the problem: Q1 capex $28.5B, FCF -$5.4B even after $11.4B of customer prepayments counted in OCF, FY26 FCF -$23.7B, FY27 capex guide $90-95B gross; Oracle sold $20B of stock via ATM in one quarter and carries ~$125B of debt (~$89B net) plus ~$260-288B of lease commitments. Credit markets are more bearish than equity: S&P BBB-, Moody's Baa2 negative, CDS ~200-219bp (18-year high), 10y yield ~6.4% vs 5.7% BBB curve, long bonds ~77c and Jupiter loans ~90c. ~Half of RPO is OpenAI, which needs ~$200B of outside capital. Litigation (class action alleging $1.8B+ insider sales; bondholder suit) is an overhang, though Ellison cancelled his 50M-share sale plan (mild positive). Valuation: CY2027 EPS ~$9.8 (5/12 FY27 $8.14 + 7/12 FY28 $11.0) -> 14.6x at $143 vs peer median 21.0x on a consistent calendar-2027 basis; I argue a persistent discount and apply 14x to a haircut forward EPS (~$148) blended 60/40 with a skeptic DCF (~$101) -> fair value ~$129. The stock has already fallen ~56% from its high and sell-side PTs average ~$238, so much of the bear case is priced; scenarios: bear $82 (30%), base $140 (45%), bull $225 (25%), mean ~$144. The ladder is a lognormal mixture over those scenarios (bear sigma 0.35, base 0.25, bull 0.27), giving a median just below spot (~$139) with a fat left tail consistent with 56% realized vol; P(>=$86) ~0.82, P(>=$143) ~0.47, P(>=$215) ~0.16. Research limited to ~15 queries; EV/EBITDA comps not collected.
